discovery: Development of massively parallel next-generation DNA sequencing (sequencing by synthesis with reversible-terminator chemistry and clonal cluster amplification)
rationale: Recent Chemistry prizes went to protein design and structure prediction (2024) and metal-organic frameworks (2025), so the committee may turn next to chemistry with large biomedical impact. Sequencing by synthesis rests on chemical innovations: fluorescent reversible terminators and surface cluster chemistry. It cut genome sequencing costs by about a million-fold and transformed biology and medicine. It has also won the Breakthrough Prize (2022) and the Millennium Technology Prize (2020), a common path to the Nobel. The main alternative is controlled radical polymerization (Matyjaszewski, Sawamoto).
